scenes.tts: The attached piece can regrow. So why does it stall in the brain and spinal cord?
scenes.visual: Title card: Drive Against Resistance. A proximal axon tip stalled at the edge of central tissue.
scenes.narration: The attached piece can regrow. So why does it stall in the brain and spinal cord?

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty-one, Samuel David and Albert Aguayo changed mainly the tissue. In adult rats, they bridged the medulla to the spinal cord with peripheral nerve.
scenes.caption: In 1981, Samuel David and Albert Aguayo changed mainly the tissue. In adult rats, they bridged the medulla to the spinal cord with peripheral nerve.
scenes.visual: Credit card: David and Aguayo, 1981. A peripheral nerve bridge is laid from the medulla to the spinal cord.
scenes.narration: In 1981, Samuel David and Albert Aguayo changed mainly the tissue. In adult rats, they bridged the medulla to the spinal cord with peripheral nerve.

scenes.tts: If adult central neurons cannot grow long axons at all, nothing grows. If the tissue stops them, what should you see?
scenes.visual: Axon tips wait at both ends of the bridge, with question marks.
scenes.narration: If adult central neurons cannot grow long axons at all, nothing grows. If the tissue stops them, what should you see?

scenes.tts: Central axons grew about thirty millimetres along the grafts. Back in central tissue, they soon stopped.
scenes.caption: Central axons grew about 30 millimetres along the grafts. Back in central tissue, they soon stopped.
scenes.visual: Axons advance along the bridge; on screen, about 30 mm. Where they re-enter the cord, they stop.
scenes.narration: Central axons grew about 30 millimetres along the grafts. Back in central tissue, they soon stopped.

scenes.tts: Now keep the central tissue, and change mainly the neuron. In two thousand eight, Zhigang He's laboratory deleted P ten from retinal ganglion cells in mice.
scenes.caption: Now keep the central tissue, and change mainly the neuron. In 2008, Zhigang He's laboratory deleted PTEN from retinal ganglion cells in mice.
scenes.visual: Credit card: He laboratory, 2008. A retina and optic nerve; PTEN crossed out in retinal ganglion cells.
scenes.narration: Now keep the central tissue, and change mainly the neuron. In 2008, Zhigang He's laboratory deleted PTEN from retinal ganglion cells in mice.

scenes.tts: P ten is a brake on cell growth. Then they crushed the optic nerve, which is central tissue. Will the axons cross?
scenes.caption: PTEN is a brake on cell growth. Then they crushed the optic nerve, which is central tissue. Will the axons cross?
scenes.visual: Label: PTEN, a brake on the mTOR growth pathway. A crush mark on the optic nerve; tips wait with a question mark.
scenes.narration: PTEN is a brake on cell growth. Then they crushed the optic nerve, which is central tissue. Will the axons cross?

scenes.tts: Some do. They come from a minority of the neurons, but far more than normal.
scenes.visual: A few axons cross the crush; a control nerve beside it has almost none.
scenes.narration: Some do. They come from a minority of the neurons, but far more than normal.

scenes.tts: So it is not a gate. Each experiment got growth while changing mainly one side. It is a balance.
scenes.visual: A gate icon is crossed out; the balance returns.
scenes.narration: So it is not a gate. Each experiment got growth while changing mainly one side. It is a balance.

scenes.tts: Picture neurons spread out by drive, and a line set by the tissue. Only neurons past the line regrow.
scenes.visual: A bell-shaped hump of neurons along a drive axis, labelled hypothetical spread, and a vertical resistance line out in its thin upper tail. A sliver past the line is lit.
scenes.narration: Picture neurons spread out by drive, and a line set by the tissue. Only neurons past the line regrow.

scenes.tts: Lower the line, or push the neurons up, and some get through. Here the line sits in the thin tail. So doing both passes more than the two gains added. With another spread, the gains might only add. This is a model, not data.
scenes.visual: The line moves left, then the hump moves right, then both; a wider band lights. On screen: an illustrative model, not data; the result depends on the spread.
scenes.narration: Lower the line, or push the neurons up, and some get through. Here the line sits in the thin tail. So doing both passes more than the two gains added. With another spread, the gains might only add. This is a model, not data.

scenes.tts: Myelin proteins such as Nogo collapse growth cones. Yet mice lacking three of them barely regrow more. Why?
scenes.visual: A growth cone collapses on myelin. Three inhibitor icons are crossed out; the axon still stalls.
scenes.narration: Myelin proteins such as Nogo collapse growth cones. Yet mice lacking three of them barely regrow more. Why?

scenes.tts: One way to see it: most neurons may sit far below the line. Lowering it a little moves few across. Other barriers remain, too.
scenes.visual: On the threshold picture, labelled one possible explanation, the line shifts slightly; almost no extra neurons cross. Other barrier icons stay in place.
scenes.narration: One way to see it: most neurons may sit far below the line. Lowering it a little moves few across. Other barriers remain, too.

scenes.tts: The scar resists, but also helps. In mice, removing its astrocyte border reduced stimulated regrowth. Change the scar, do not remove it.
scenes.visual: A lesion ringed by astrocytes. The ring is removed; stimulated axons grow less. Label: change it, do not remove it.
scenes.narration: The scar resists, but also helps. In mice, removing its astrocyte border reduced stimulated regrowth. Change the scar, do not remove it.

scenes.tts: And regrowth is not recovery. At a steady millimetre a day, a metre takes about a thousand days, nearly three years. Over that long a time, Schwann cells lose their repair state, and distant targets are hard to reach.
scenes.visual: A ruler from the spinal cord to a toe. On screen: 1 m at a steady 1 mm a day, about 1,000 days, before any delay. A repair-support bar along the ruler fades gradually as the tip advances.
scenes.narration: And regrowth is not recovery. At a steady millimetre a day, a metre takes about a thousand days, nearly three years. Over that long a time, Schwann cells lose their repair state, and distant targets are hard to reach.

scenes.tts: Blocking Sarm one may help failing axons that are still attached. A fully severed stump cannot rejoin its cell body on its own.
scenes.caption: Blocking SARM1 may help failing axons that are still attached. A fully severed stump cannot rejoin its cell body on its own.
scenes.visual: Split screen: a connected, failing axon protected by a SARM1 blocker; a severed stump, preserved by the blocker alone, that stays apart.
scenes.narration: Blocking SARM1 may help failing axons that are still attached. A fully severed stump cannot rejoin its cell body on its own.

scenes.tts: For regrowth, no single fix is enough. None yet restores function reliably in people.
scenes.visual: Icons: Nogo blocker, scar enzyme, growth boost, bridge. Each moves the balance a little.
scenes.narration: For regrowth, no single fix is enough. None yet restores function reliably in people.

scenes.tts: One cut, two fates. A program for the cut-off piece, and a balance of drive against resistance for the attached one.
scenes.visual: Closing card: the guiding idea, both lines. Small label under the second line: a rule of thumb, not a measured quantity.
scenes.narration: One cut, two fates. A program for the cut-off piece, and a balance of drive against resistance for the attached one.
